title: Large Bricks and Join-irreducible torsionfree classes

candidates.error_location: Proof of Proposition 3.9 (application of Lemma 3.6 to a spanning tree)
candidates.exact_quote: This gives a directed system of $f$−simples consisting of monomorphisms (we don't have any compatibility condition to check on the maps as the underlying graph is a tree), therefore we can use Lemma 3.6 to obtain a $\varinjlim f$−simple $F$
candidates.claim_content: Setting: Λ is a finite-dimensional algebra, f ⊆ Λ-mod a torsionfree class, (t,f) the corresponding torsion pair. An object 0 ≠ B of f is called f-simple if all its proper quotients lie in t. The set simp(f) of (isoclasses of) f-simples is a monobrick: any non-zero map between two f-simples is a monomorphism, and B ≺ B' means there is a monomorphism B → B'. Lemma 3.6 of the paper states: if {F_i, (α_ij)} is a DIRECT system (directed/filtered index set) of non-zero maps between f-simple modules, then F = lim_→ {F_i,(α_ij)} is lim_→ f -simple; its proof uses filteredness twice (every canonical map F_i → F is mono, and every map from a finite-dimensional module S into F factors through some F_i). In Proposition 3.9 the author takes a spanning tree T of the underlying graph of the Hasse quiver of the poset simp(f), orients its edges by the Hasse quiver orientation to get an acyclic quiver T', chooses a module V_i for each vertex and a non-zero map V_i → V_j for each edge v_i → v_j, and then asserts that this is a 'directed system' to which Lemma 3.6 applies, concluding that the colimit F is lim_→ f -simple and that every f-simple embeds in F.
candidates.suspected_defect: A tree (even with the Hasse orientation) is in general NOT a directed/filtered diagram: two vertices of the tree joined by a zig-zag path need have no common successor inside the tree. Hence the colimit over T' is not a direct limit, Lemma 3.6 (stated and proved for filtered systems) does not apply, and the key steps of its proof (factoring maps from finite-dimensional modules through some V_i; canonical maps being monomorphisms) are unavailable. The whole conclusion of Proposition 3.9 rests on this step.

candidates.error_location: Proof of Proposition 3.9 (properties of the colimit over the tree)
candidates.exact_quote: therefore we can use Lemma 3.6 to obtain a $\varinjlim f$−simple $F$ with the property that every $f$−simple is isomorphic to a submodule of $F$
candidates.claim_content: Claim to be checked: let D be a diagram of Λ-modules indexed by a connected acyclic quiver (tree) whose arrows are all monomorphisms between f-simple modules (f a torsionfree class in Λ-mod, f-simple = non-zero object of f all of whose proper quotients lie in the torsion class t). Let F = colim D. The paper asserts (i) every V_i maps monomorphically into F, so that every f-simple is isomorphic to a submodule of F, and (ii) F lies in lim_→ f and every proper quotient of F lies in lim_→ t (i.e. F is lim_→ f -simple).
candidates.suspected_defect: Colimits over a non-filtered tree are computed by iterated pushouts, i.e. by cokernels; torsionfree classes (and their direct limit closures) are closed under submodules, extensions and direct limits, but NOT under cokernels/pushouts. So there is no reason for the tree colimit F to lie in lim_→ f, let alone to be lim_→ f -simple. Statement (i) also needs a separate argument (pushouts of monos) that is not given. Neither (i) nor (ii) is covered by Lemma 3.6, which is stated for filtered direct systems.

candidates.error_location: Last line of the proof of Proposition 3.9
candidates.exact_quote: So we obtain that $f = \mathbf{F}(B)\cap \Lambda\text{−mod}$ by Theorem 2.5.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: f is a join-irreducible torsionfree class in Λ-mod (Λ finite-dimensional algebra), simp(f) is the set of f-simples, and Theorem 2.5 (Enomoto) says f = filt(simp(f)), where filt denotes closure under extensions. The proof of Proposition 3.9 produces a module B ∈ Λ-Mod, torsionfree almost torsion for the cosilting torsion pair (lim_→ t, lim_→ f), together with a module F such that every f-simple embeds into F and F embeds into B; hence every f-simple lies in cogen(B). From this the author concludes f = F(B) ∩ Λ-mod, where F(B) is never defined in the paper (presumably the torsionfree class cogenerated by B, i.e. modules embedding into products/coproducts of copies of B).
candidates.suspected_defect: Theorem 2.5 only gives f = filt(simp(f)) ⊆ filt(cogen(B)), which is in general strictly larger than cogen(B): the class of modules cogenerated by B need not be closed under extensions, so the inclusion f ⊆ F(B) is not established if F(B) means cogen(B) (as the abstract's phrase 'cogenerated by a single brick' suggests). Moreover the reverse inclusion F(B) ∩ Λ-mod ⊆ f is not argued at all. The undefined symbol F(B) makes the final equality unverifiable as written.

candidates.exact_quote: Then there exists a brick $B$ in $\Lambda\text{−Mod}$ which is torsionfree, almost torsion for $\varinjlim f$
candidates.claim_content: Proposition 3.9 asserts the existence of a BRICK B (End_Λ(B) a skew field) in Λ-Mod which is torsionfree, almost torsion for the torsion pair (lim_→ t, lim_→ f). The proof (via Lemma 3.7) only produces a module B which is a simple object of the heart H of the HRS-tilt, equivalently (Proposition 3.5) torsionfree almost torsion; no verification that End_Λ(B) is a division ring is given.
candidates.suspected_defect: The brick property is asserted but never proved; it needs the identification End_H(B) = End_Λ(B) for B in the torsionfree class F together with Schur's lemma in the heart. Possibly true, but it is an unjustified step in the statement's proof.

candidates.error_location: Proof of Lemma 3.6 (reduction to maximal quotients)
candidates.exact_quote: Using the fact that torsion classes are closed under quotients, this task can be reduced to proving that every maximal quotient of F is a torsion module.
candidates.claim_content: Lemma 3.6 asks to show that every proper quotient F/X (X ≠ 0 a submodule of the possibly infinite-dimensional module F = lim_→ F_i) lies in the torsion class lim_→ t. The proof reduces this to showing that every 'maximal quotient' of F (i.e. F/S with S a simple submodule, obtained from a non-zero map S → F with S simple) is in lim_→ t, invoking closure of torsion classes under quotients.
candidates.suspected_defect: Closure under quotients goes the wrong way for a naive reading: F/X is NOT a quotient of a maximal quotient unless one knows that every non-zero submodule X of F contains a simple submodule S (so that F/X is a quotient of F/S). This fact (true over an artinian ring, since any non-zero cyclic submodule has finite length) is never stated, and the written reduction as such ('maximal quotient torsion ⇒ all proper quotients torsion') does not follow from closure under quotients alone.

candidates.exact_quote: thus it must be that B ∈ cogen(v ∪ w) that is B ∈ v or B ∈ w
candidates.claim_content: Setting: v, w are torsionfree classes in Λ-mod contained in a torsionfree class f with f = v ∨ w; cogen(E) denotes the objects embeddable in a FINITE coproduct of objects of E; B is an f-simple object (0 ≠ B ∈ f, all proper quotients of B lie in the torsion class t). The proof asserts that B ∈ cogen(v ∪ w) implies B ∈ v or B ∈ w.
candidates.suspected_defect: B ∈ cogen(v ∪ w) only says B embeds into a finite direct sum V ⊕ W with V ∈ v, W ∈ w; membership in v or in w requires the extra argument that one of the induced maps B → V, B → W is injective (which uses f-simplicity again: the image B/ker is a torsionfree quotient, hence either 0 or B). The implication is stated as immediate and the supporting argument is omitted; as written the step does not follow.

candidates.exact_quote: f is completely join irreducible if and only if the monobrick of f-simple modules is directed and has finite height (i.e. it has a maximum)
candidates.claim_content: Corollary 2.10 claims, for a torsionfree class f in Λ-mod with poset simp(f) of f-simples (ordered by existence of a monomorphism), that complete join-irreducibility of f is equivalent to simp(f) being directed (every finite subset has an upper bound) and of finite height, and parenthetically that 'directed and of finite height' is the same as 'has a maximum'.
candidates.suspected_defect: The parenthetical equivalence is not a general poset fact: a poset with a maximum is directed but need not have finite height (e.g. an infinite ascending chain with a top added). The equivalence only holds because in Λ-mod the order is by embeddings and all elements are finite-dimensional, so a maximum bounds all dimensions; this is not stated. Also the claimed equivalence 'completely join irreducible ⇔ f = filtcogen(B) for a finitely generated brick B, and B is f-simple' is asserted as 'a standard computation' without proof.

candidates.exact_quote:
When R is a left noetherian ring, there is a bijection

tors(R) ↔ Cosilt(R).
candidates.claim_content: The paper states: for a left noetherian ring R there is a bijection between the set tors(R) of torsion pairs in R-mod and the set Cosilt(R) of torsion pairs in R-Mod cogenerated by a cosilting module, given by (t,f) ↦ (lim_→ t, lim_→ f) = (Gen t, t^{⊥_0}), with inverse (T,F) ↦ (T ∩ R-mod, F ∩ R-mod).
candidates.suspected_defect: In the literature the bijection with torsion pairs in R-mod is usually with cosilting classes OF COFINITE TYPE; it is not clear (and is open/false in general for non-commutative noetherian rings) that every cosilting torsion pair over a left noetherian ring is of cofinite type, so the surjectivity half of the stated bijection may be an overstatement of the cited result.

candidates.error_location: Abstract vs. Notation section and proofs (scope of hypotheses)
candidates.exact_quote: We show that every join-irreducible torsionfree class in the category of finitely generated modules over an artinian ring is cogenerated by a single (not necessarily finitely generated) brick.
candidates.claim_content: The abstract claims the result for finitely generated modules over an arbitrary artinian ring, while the Notation section fixes Λ to be a finite-dimensional k-algebra over a field k, and Proposition 3.9 (the main result) is stated and proved for Λ-mod with Λ finite-dimensional. Several steps use finite dimensionality explicitly: Lemma 3.6 ('As S is a finite-dimensional module, any map from S to F can be factored through the direct system'), the remark that a monobrick poset has countable height because 'only countably many dimensions of finite-dimensional modules', and Proposition 3.9 ('As all the isoclasses involved correspond to finite-dimensional modules, the poset of objects smaller than F_3 has finite height').
candidates.suspected_defect: The hypotheses actually used (finite-dimensional algebra over a field, finite-dimensional modules) are stronger than those claimed in the abstract (arbitrary artinian ring); the arguments as written (dimension counts, finite-dimensionality for finite presentation) are not carried out for general artinian rings. Also the conclusion 'cogenerated by a single brick' does not literally match the conclusion f = F(B) ∩ Λ-mod of Proposition 3.9, where F(B) is undefined.

candidates.exact_quote: We therefore have a non-zero map F → S which must be a monomorphism, by simplicity of F.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: F is a lim_→ f -simple module (non-zero, in the cosilting torsionfree class F = lim_→ f, with every proper quotient in the torsion class T = lim_→ t); S is a simple object of the heart H of the HRS-tilt which is torsion with respect to (F, T[−1]), hence by Proposition 3.5 a torsionfree almost torsion module; there is an epimorphism F → S in H. The paper concludes that the induced map F → S is a monomorphism of modules.
candidates.suspected_defect: Two implicit steps: (a) an epimorphism in the heart H need not be a module epimorphism, and one must know Hom_H(F,S) = Hom_Λ(F,S) for modules in the torsionfree class; (b) the monomorphism conclusion uses not only simplicity of F but also that S is torsionfree (so that the torsion quotient F/ker, if proper, cannot embed in S). Neither is justified in the text.

candidates.exact_quote: Then we can find f-simples B₁, B₂ such that B₁↑ := {B ∈ simp(f) | B₁ ≺ B} and B₂↑ are disjoint.
candidates.claim_content: Definition used: a nonempty poset P is directed if every finite subset has an upper bound. The proof asserts that if the nonempty poset simp(f) of f-simples is not directed, then there exist two elements B₁, B₂ whose up-sets B₁↑ and B₂↑ are disjoint (i.e. the pair {B₁,B₂} has no upper bound).
candidates.suspected_defect: Non-directedness literally says some finite subset has no upper bound; the reduction to a two-element subset requires the standard induction (if every pair has an upper bound then every finite nonempty subset does), which is not mentioned. Likely harmless, but the stated inference is not immediate from the definition given.
